'''Sean Christopher Williams''' (born September 13, 1986) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player.

==Early years==
Sean Williams grew up in suburban [[Arlington, Texas]], with his mother and stepfather, Audrey and Lawrence Garrett, and his two half-siblings: [[Myles Garrett|Myles]] and Brea Garrett. Myles played football at [[Texas A&M University]] and was the No. 1 overall pick in the [[2017 NFL Draft|2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://nba.nbcsports.com/2017/04/28/did-you-know-myles-garrett-no-1-pick-in-nfl-draft-has-brother-who-played-in-nba/|title=Did you know Myles Garrett, No. 1 pick in NFL draft, has brother who played in NBA?|last=Feldman|first=Dan|date=2017-04-28|website=ProBasketballTalk|access-date=2017-04-29}}</ref> Sean's father, Roland Williams, lives in [[Houston]], [[Texas]]. Sean did not play organized basketball until he was 15 years old. He became a local standout in community leagues and eventually began playing basketball for [[Mansfield High School (Mansfield, Texas)|Mansfield High School]] in [[Mansfield, Texas]].

==College career==
As a member of the [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College basketball]] team, Williams began his career as a standout in the paint. He functioned as an intimidating shot-blocking force for his team. Some basketball games were dubbed the "Sean Williams Block Party".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/web/COM1041644/index.htm|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130119151700/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/web/COM1041644/index.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 19, 2013|title=March Madness, March Badness|publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=March 2, 2005}}</ref> Despite having never played an entire season for Boston College (BC), Williams left the university as a leading shot blocker in the [[Big East Conference]] and [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]], respectively, during each of his BC seasons. Williams established himself as the nation's top college shot blocker by breaking his own record when he blocked 75 shots in only 15 games during the 2006–2007 season.

Williams was dismissed from the Boston College basketball team during his junior year after having been suspended twice during his three-year college basketball career for multiple rules violations, including an arrest for [[Cannabis (drug)|marijuana]] possession in 2005.<ref name="ESPN">{{cite web |date=17 March 2009 |title=Nets' Williams arrested after altercation |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3988374 |access-date=June 7, 2026 |website=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> During his suspension from BC for one semester during his sophomore year, Williams took classes at the [[University of Houston]].

==Professional career==

===NBA and NBA D-League career===

====New Jersey Nets====
Williams was selected 17th overall in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[New Jersey Nets]]. In February 2009, he was arrested while attempting to attend a BC-[[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] game in February 2009 for allegedly violating a no-trespassing order. The police report stated he was belligerent while being arrested, writing obscenities instead of his name on the fingerprint card and trespass warning.<ref name="ESPN"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nj.com/nets/index.ssf/2009/02/nj_nets_the_sean_matter.html|title=New Jersey Nets: The Sean Williams Matter -- Hold Yer Fire|work=NJ.com|date=February 17, 2009 |access-date=February 18, 2017}}</ref>

On March 16, 2009, Williams was arrested and charged with [[disorderly conduct]] and [[criminal mischief]] after an altercation with the clerk at a cell phone store at Park Meadows Mall in [[Lone Tree, CO|Lone Tree, Colorado]], that ended with Williams smashing the store's computer monitor.<ref>[https://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20090317/ap_on_sp_bk_ne/bkn_nets_williams_arrested;_ylt=AucMrO8hqkRcT.sFYNQ7qFELMxIF Nets Williams Arrested After Altercation] Yahoo Sports, March 16, 2009</ref> He did not accompany his team on their flight back to New Jersey<ref>[http://www.nj.com/nets/index.ssf/2009/03/new_jersey_nets_sean_williams_2.html New Jersey Nets' Sean Williams Arrested]. NJ.com. Retrieved on April 7, 2012.</ref> and was later suspended by the team for two games.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3993959 Nets Suspend Williams] ESPN, March 18, 2009</ref> He was arrested on suspicion of disorderly conduct and felony criminal mischief.<ref name="ESPN"/>

====Colorado 14ers====
On December 29, 2008, Williams was assigned to the [[Colorado 14ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]] (D-League).<ref>[http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=501566] {{dead link|date=April 2012}}</ref> On January 22, 2009, the Nets recalled Williams from the Colorado 14ers.<ref>{{cite web | date=January 22, 2009 | title=Nets recall center Sean Williams from D-League | url=http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=509940 | access-date=January 27, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090127042229/http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=509940 |archive-date=January 27, 2009 }}</ref> On January 11, 2010, he was released by the Nets.<ref>{{cite web | title = Nets Waive Sean Williams | url = http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Sean_Williams_Waiver_Release_100111.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = January 11, 2010 | access-date = January 12, 2010}}</ref>

===International career===

====Fujian SBS XunXin====
After being released by the Nets, Williams went to play for the [[Fujian SBS Xunxing|Fujian SBS XunXin]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He played 16 games from February 5 to March 28, 2010, averaging 16.4 points, 11.1 rebounds (4.1 Off), 1.2 assists and 4.2 blocked shots.<ref name="latinbasket1">[http://www.latinbasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=PUR&PlayerID=58498 Eurobasket]. Latinbasket.com. Retrieved on April 7, 2012.</ref> Some of his notable performances in the CBA include 30 points against [[Qingdao DoubleStar|Qingdao DS]] on March 12, 2010, and 13 blocks against [[Jilin Northeast Tigers|Jilin]] on February 26, 2010. Williams also won the 2010 CBA All Star Game Dunk contest. The event was held at the [[LeSports Center|Wukesong Stadium]] in [[Beijing|Beijing, China]], on March 21.<ref>[http://dunkcontest.free.fr/index.php?post/2010/03/25/Sean-Williams-Wins-CBA-Dunk-Contest Sean Williams Wins CBA Dunk Contest – Dunk Contest – The Ultimate Slam Dunk Contest Resource] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720221021/http://dunkcontest.free.fr/index.php?post%2F2010%2F03%2F25%2FSean-Williams-Wins-CBA-Dunk-Contest |date=July 20, 2011 }}. Dunk Contest (2010-03-25). Retrieved on April 7, 2012.</ref>

====Guaynabo Mets====
Williams landed in [[Puerto Rico]] to end his 2009–10 season, joining the [[Guaynabo Mets|Mets de Guaynabo]], where he averaged 10.0 pts and 16.5 rebounds in 2 games.<ref name="latinbasket1"/>

====Maccabi Haifa====
In August 2010, Williams was signed by [[Hapoel Jerusalem]], but he was released before his first game in the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli league]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/69086/20100912/sean_williams_released_by_hapoel/ | title=NBA News, Rumors, NCAA Basketball, Euroleague | work=RealGM | access-date=April 7, 2012 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101115122958/http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/69086/20100912/sean_williams_released_by_hapoel | archive-date=November 15, 2010 | df=mdy-all }}</ref> After a season in the NBA and the D-League, Williams returned to [[Israel]]. On August 10, 2011, he signed a two-year contract with [[Maccabi Haifa B.C.]], which included an out clause that would have enabled him to return to the NBA when the [[2011 NBA lockout]] ended, and if he received an NBA offer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4680657/sources-legends-sean-williams-to-israel|title=Sources: Legends' Sean Williams to Israel|work=ESPN.go.com|date=August 10, 2011 |access-date=February 18, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|maWLr5nNCyY|Sean Williams highlights in Israel}}</ref>

===Return to the NBA/NBA D-League===

====Texas Legends====
In November 2010, after playing in Puerto Rico and China, Williams joined the [[Texas Legends]] of the D-League. He played 49 games during the 2010–11 regular season (46 games as a starter), averaging 14.4 pts, 2.9 blocks, 9.4 rebounds and 0.8 steals per game.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/sean_williams/index.html?nav=page Sean Williams D-League playerfile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101124224529/http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/sean_williams/index.html?nav=page |date=November 24, 2010 }}. NBA.com (1986-09-13). Retrieved on April 7, 2012.</ref> He was selected to the 2011 NBA D-League All-Star Game, along with his Legends teammate [[Joe Alexander]]. Williams earned a spot in the 2011 All-NBA Development League Third Team and also ranked second in voting for the Defensive Player of the Year category. Williams had more first place votes than [[Chris Johnson (basketball, born 1985)|Chris Johnson]], but Johnson still won the award.<ref>Schroeder, Scott. (2011-04-22) [http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2011/4/22/2126153/2011-nba-d-league-award-winners-curtis-stinson-trey-johnson 2011 NBA D-League Award Winners: We Have Vote Totals!]. Ridiculous Upside. Retrieved on April 7, 2012.</ref>

====Dallas Mavericks====
On December 21, 2011, he signed a two-year contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4682325/sean-williams-officially-signs-with-mavs Sean Williams officially signs with Mavs] ESPN, December 21, 2011</ref> The Mavericks then assigned him to the [[Texas Legends]] of the D-League.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/dleague/transactions.html 2011–12 Transactions] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111101144313/http://www.nba.com/dleague/dleague/transactions.html |date=November 1, 2011 }}. Nba.com. Retrieved on April 7, 2012.</ref> Williams played his first game for the Mavericks in their 115–93 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]] on December 26, 2011, providing some much needed spark off the bench in the 3rd quarter. Williams went 4–4 from the field, which included two high flying alley-oops, and 4–4 from the free throw line and picked up 3 rebounds, a steal and a block in his 11 minutes of game time.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20111226/DENDAL/gameinfo.html?ls=gt2hp0021100012#nbaGIboxscore Games]. NBA.com. Retrieved on 2012-04-07.</ref> As he was leaving the court in the fourth quarter, he threw up on the Mavericks bench.<ref>[http://sportsblogs.star-telegram.com/mavs/2011/12/williams-throws-down-then-up.html Full-Court Press: Williams throws down, then up] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120108093500/http://sportsblogs.star-telegram.com/mavs/2011/12/williams-throws-down-then-up.html |date=January 8, 2012 }}. Sportsblogs.star-telegram.com (2011-12-26). Retrieved on April 7, 2012.</ref>

====Return to the Texas Legends====
On January 6, 2012, Williams was reassigned to the [[Texas Legends]], along with [[Yi Jianlian]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/dallas_mavericks_assign_yi_jia_2012_01_06.html Dallas Mavericks Assign Yi Jianlian to Texas Legends] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120227145702/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/dallas_mavericks_assign_yi_jia_2012_01_06.html |date=February 27, 2012 }}. Nba.com (2012-01-06). Retrieved on April 7, 2012.</ref>

====Return to Dallas====
On March 4, 2012, Williams was recalled by the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>[http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/dallas-mavericks/headlines/20120304-mavericks-recall-sean-williams-from-d-league-as-brandan-wright-recovers-from-friday-s-concussion.ece Mavericks recall Sean Williams from D-League as Brandan Wright recovers from Friday's concussion]. Dallasnews.com (2012-03-04). Retrieved on 2012-04-07.</ref> After being recalled for the maximum third time from March 16 to 18, Williams was waived by the Mavericks on March 22, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web | author=Jeff Caplan | date=March 22, 2012 | title=Mavs waive goodbye to Sean Williams - Dallas Mavericks Blog- ESPN | url=http://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4686997/mavs-waive-goodbye-to-sean-williams | website=ESPN.com | access-date=February 18, 2017}}</ref>

====Boston Celtics====
On April 20, 2012, Williams was signed by the [[Boston Celtics]], returning to the city where he played college basketball.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/042012-sign-williams-waive-oneal.html|title=Celtics Waive O'Neal, Sign Sean Williams - The Official Site of the BOSTON CELTICS|work=NBA.com|access-date=February 18, 2017}}</ref> On July 5, 2012, the Celtics announced that Williams was added to their roster for the 2012 Orlando Pro Summer League and the 2012 [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.weei.com/sports/boston/this-just-in/21211731/rookies-williams-cs-summer-league-roster|title=Sean Williams on C's summer league roster|author=Paul Flannery|date=July 5, 2012|work=WEEI.com|access-date=February 18, 2017}}</ref>

====Houston Rockets====
On July 20, 2012, Williams was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in a three team deal.<ref>{{cite web | title = Rockets Get Players And Pick In Three-Team Deal | url = http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-get-players-and-pick-three-team-deal |work=NBA.com | date=July 20, 2012 | access-date =July 20, 2012}}</ref> He was waived by the Rockets on August 29, 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10836|title=Houston Rockets waive forward Sean Williams :InsideHoops|author=Inside Hoops|date=August 29, 2012|work=InsideHoops.com|access-date=February 18, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130206100625/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10836|archive-date=February 6, 2013|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

====Return to Texas Legends====
Williams was re-acquired by the Legends on December 10, 2012.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/dleague/transactions.html 2012-13 Transactions] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111101144313/http://www.nba.com/dleague/dleague/transactions.html |date=November 1, 2011 }}</ref>

====Delaware 87ers====
On August 29, 2013, Williams' rights were acquired by the [[Delaware 87ers]] in the 2013 NBA Development League Expansion Draft.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/87ers_expansion_draft_2013_08_29.html NBA Development League Announced 2013 Expansion Draft Results] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204005548/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/87ers_expansion_draft_2013_08_29.html |date=December 4, 2013 }}</ref>

===Turkey===
In September 2013, he joined [[Torku Konyaspor B.K.|Torku Selçuk Üniversitesi]] of the [[Turkish Basketball League]].

===Philippines===
In March 2017, he signed with the [[GlobalPort Batang Pier]] as their import for the [[2017 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://pba.ph/news/2-nba-vets-coming-for-2017-pba-commissioner-s-cup |title=2 NBA Vets Coming For 2017 PBA Commissioner's Cup |publisher=pba.ph |publication-date=March 10, 2017 |access-date=March 10, 2017}}</ref> He was then replaced after playing only three games.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/news/globalport-set-to-bring-in-new-import-malcolm-white-as-losses-keep-piling-up-in-commissioners-cup- |title=GlobalPort brings in new import Malcolm White to replace Williams as losses pile up |last=Ramos |first=Gerry |date=April 7, 2017 |publisher=spin.ph |access-date=April 7, 2017}}</ref>
